text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Tuesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The new ambassador to Ukraine says the ambassador before him squandered funds by having too large an embassy.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas suggested to parliament to dismiss prosecutor general Vladas Nikitinas and to appoint his deputy Arturas Paulauskas to the post on a temporary basis.
- Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal said on Monday in Vilnius that Lithuania has made big progress and has a good chance to integrate into European structures.

- The transport ministry intends to merge Lithuanian Airlines and Aviation company Lietuva and only then start the privatisation. The state should keep control of no less than 50 percent of the shares.

- Agricultural Bank has signed a protocol of intention with Central European Media Enterprises a few months ago to sell its stake in commercial LNK television. The bank wants to sell its shares for $7 million but the buyer has not agreed to pay this sum. Negotiations are continuing.

- Transport Minister Algis Zvaliauskas is worried that the renovation of Zokniu airport near Siauliai have attracted little foreign investment and are financed from a $30 million credit taken by Siauliai local council.
- Russian secret services are connected to the Lithuanian banking crisis, said the minister of Poland's secret services in an article in Rzeczpospolita on Saturday.
- The support of the U.S Congress to the Baltic states and their independance was and is very big, said U.S. congressman Richard Durbin in an interview to the newspaper.
- Brazauskas will read his 99-page annual speech in parliament today, where much attention will be paid to a survey of the country's economy.

- Although the Constitutional court said last week that the ban on alcohol and tobacco advertising did not contradict the constitution, alcohol and tobacco continues to be advertised as parliament has to decide what is information and what is advertising.
- Preliminary statistics show that Lithuania's foreign trade deficit in January-November 1996 was 3.77 billion litas, 481 million litas more than in the same period in 1995.
